response.sql: WITH fee_ord AS (SELECT f.orderslink, o.dealedge, f.feerate - f.rebrate AS net_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 AND o.dealedge IS NOT NULL), group_avg AS (SELECT orderslink, dealedge AS side, AVG(net_rate) AS avg_net_rate, COUNT(net_rate) AS record_count FROM fee_ord GROUP BY orderslink, dealedge), side_avg AS (SELECT side, AVG(avg_net_rate) AS side_avg FROM group_avg GROUP BY side) SELECT g.orderslink, g.side, g.avg_net_rate, g.record_count, g.avg_net_rate - s.side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg FROM group_avg g JOIN side_avg s ON g.side = s.side WHERE g.avg_net_rate > s.side_avg ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A fee row's net rate is NULL, and so excluded from the average, when either feerate or rebrate is NULL. Only rows with feerate >= 0.0009 are considered, so NULL feerate is already excluded.
record_count counts only records with a non-NULL net rate, so it matches the records that feed the average.
orders.recordvault is unique, so the inner join does not duplicate fee rows.
Orders with a NULL dealedge are excluded, since they have no side to group or average under.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat a missing rebrate as zero rebate, so the net rate equals feerate for those rows instead of dropping them from the average.
alternatives.sql: WITH fee_ord AS (SELECT f.orderslink, o.dealedge, f.feerate - COALESCE(f.rebrate, 0) AS net_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 AND o.dealedge IS NOT NULL), group_avg AS (SELECT orderslink, dealedge AS side, AVG(net_rate) AS avg_net_rate, COUNT(net_rate) AS record_count FROM fee_ord GROUP BY orderslink, dealedge), side_avg AS (SELECT side, AVG(avg_net_rate) AS side_avg FROM group_avg GROUP BY side) SELECT g.orderslink, g.side, g.avg_net_rate, g.record_count, g.avg_net_rate - s.side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg FROM group_avg g JOIN side_avg s ON g.side = s.side WHERE g.avg_net_rate > s.side_avg ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

alternatives.interpretation: Count every fee record in the group, including those whose net rate is missing, rather than only the records that contribute to the average.
alternatives.sql: WITH fee_ord AS (SELECT f.orderslink, o.dealedge, f.feerate - f.rebrate AS net_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 AND o.dealedge IS NOT NULL), group_avg AS (SELECT orderslink, dealedge AS side, AVG(net_rate) AS avg_net_rate, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM fee_ord GROUP BY orderslink, dealedge), side_avg AS (SELECT side, AVG(avg_net_rate) AS side_avg FROM group_avg GROUP BY side) SELECT g.orderslink, g.side, g.avg_net_rate, g.record_count, g.avg_net_rate - s.side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg FROM group_avg g JOIN side_avg s ON g.side = s.side WHERE g.avg_net_rate > s.side_avg ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
